method_notes.pooled_w10: the current method (study 1's choice): 10 consecutive calibration origins
method_notes.spread_y1: calibration origins spread over the last year: weekly 26 origins 2 weeks apart, daily 52 origins 7 days apart (hypothesis from study 1: consecutive daily origins give one series too few, too similar scores)

development.nordwerk_a: NordWerk seed 20260928: cross-validation origins only (as study 1)
development.uci_retail: UCI Online Retail II weekly, 50 products: cross-validation origins only (as study 1)
development.nordwerk_b: NordWerk seed 20261015 (study 1's test set, now seen): cross-validation and holdout origins
development.bike_daily: UCI Bike Sharing daily (study 1's test set, now seen): cross-validation and holdout origins

test.nordwerk_c: a NEW NordWerk realisation, seed 20261101 (synthetic, weekly): all origins
test.smard_areas: SMARD daily electricity consumption (grid load) of the four German control areas 50Hertz, Amprion, TenneT, TransnetBW, 2019-01-01 to the last published day at retrieval (real, CC BY 4.0, Bundesnetzagentur | SMARD.de): all origins; no interval study has used these series

study.selection: among methods whose development coverage is within 0.75..0.85 on ALL FOUR development datasets, the lowest mean scaled interval score (mean over the four); if none qualifies, the method with the most development datasets inside 0.75..0.85 (ties: lowest mean scaled interval score) is tested, and can at best be reported, not validated
study.validation: the selected method is 'validated on these datasets' only if it qualified on development AND its test coverage is within 0.75..0.85 on BOTH test datasets; otherwise ranges stay labelled not validated and nothing may rely on them
study.reported: per dataset and method: points n, series, origins, empirical coverage, mean scaled width, mean scaled interval score (alpha 0.2, study 1's definition), coverage by horizon
study.not_allowed: no change of rules, methods, datasets or thresholds after seeing development or test results
